question: What is the consequence of a high apparent volume of distribution of a drug?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: High apparent volume of distribution -> Low drug concentration in plasma -> Lower pharmacological effect -> 80% CHAIN: High apparent volume of distribution -> Increased drug distribution in tissues -> Delayed elimination -> Greater pharmacological effect -> 70% CHAIN: High apparent volume of distribution -> Increased binding to tissues -> Reduced free drug concentration -> Lower pharmacological effect -> 75% CHAIN: High apparent volume of distribution -> Increased binding to plasma proteins -> Lower free drug concentration -> Lower pharmacological effect -> 80%
analysis: A high apparent volume of distribution of a drug indicates that the drug is extensively distributed throughout the body tissues rather than staying primarily in the plasma. This can lead to a lower concentration in the plasma.
